destination.title: Corrections to black holes and branes: extremality, response and consistency
destination.question: How do higher-derivative, nonlinear and quantum corrections change black-hole or brane observables, and which source-specific assumptions support consistency bounds?
destination.summary: This is a proposed organization of candidate numerical memberships. Extremality, entropy, force, transport, tidal response and damping are distinct targets. Their shared methods justify navigation between questions without identifying their assumptions or conclusions.

systems: Black holes and charged black branes in the supplied gravitational theories
Axionic semiwormholes and quantum-corrected RN-AdS Kiselev backgrounds as comparison directions
targets: Transport, tidal response and quasinormal spectra
Conditional UV-consistency, discharge and censorship diagnostics
regimes: One-loop running and explicitly nonlocal corrections
Nonlinear electromagnetic field dependence beyond leading truncation
Extremal, near-extremal and other explicitly specified backgrounds
assumptions: WGC variants, entropy positivity, duality, supersymmetry and causality criteria remain distinct conditional inputs or research targets.
Numerical membership supplies no scientific implication or equivalence.
conventions: Keep mass-to-charge and charge-to-mass sign conventions separate.
Retain each source's fixed thermodynamic quantities, charge normalization and perturbative order.
Proposed singleton identities retain the exact supplied question; they do not establish cross-source uniqueness.
includes: Ordinary gravitational EFT and holographic work without a Swampland premise
Source-scoped historical hypotheses and proposed counterexample searches
Alternate homes for related questions outside the local black-hole EFT core
excludes: A universal equivalence among extremality, entropy positivity and self-repulsion
Automatic identification of transport or QNM criteria with the WGC
Treating proposed extensions or background-dependent bounds as established universal results

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Reissner--Nordström Black Holes from Worldline QFT

evidence.text: How do four-derivative curvature–Maxwell couplings modify electrically charged Reissner–Nordström geometry, extremality and entropy, and can worldline QFT recover these corrections and support shadow constraints?

sources.title: Non-vanishing of tidal Love numbers

evidence.text: Does a cubic Riemann-curvature correction generate nonzero static black-hole tidal Love numbers, and can its correction to Wald entropy yield a controlled restriction on the coupling's sign?

sources.title: Non-vanishing of tidal Love numbers

evidence.text: Match asymptotic metric coefficients to applied tidal fields and induced multipoles. Separately apply Wald's curvature-derivative entropy formula, including both the explicit higher-curvature contribution and the perturbative shift of horizon area.

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Reissner--Nordström Black Holes from Worldline QFT

evidence.text: Construct conserved off-shell graviton and photon currents from heavy charged-scalar worldlines glued to bulk connected trees, then Fourier transform to obtain classical fields. Classical terms use no contractions between worldline emission vertices; scaleless integrals vanish in dimensional regularisation.

sources.title: Non-vanishing of tidal Love numbers

evidence.text: Expand the metric in powers of α and solve Einstein's equations with the cubic-curvature tensor evaluated on the unperturbed Schwarzschild geometry at first order. The authors also list higher-order background coefficients without obtaining an exact solution.

sources.title: Non-vanishing of tidal Love numbers

evidence.text: Decompose linear tidal perturbations into spherical harmonics and even/odd sectors in Regge–Wheeler gauge. Use the undeformed Einstein equations to replace higher derivatives, then solve the corrected radial equations with horizon regularity.

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Reissner--Nordström Black Holes from Worldline QFT

evidence.text: Determine entropy by integrating the first law using surface gravity and horizon electric potential, and separately evaluate Iyer–Wald entropy. Estimate shadows from the corrected metric's photon sphere.

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Reissner--Nordström Black Holes from Worldline QFT

evidence.text: Solve modified Einstein–Maxwell equations perturbatively in the higher-derivative couplings using ds²=−N²f dt²+dr²/f+r²dΩ². Impose asymptotic boundary conditions fixing mass and charge, then transform to de Donder coordinates to compare with the worldline expansion.

sources.title: Locality Outside Extremal Black Holes

evidence.text: Must local higher-derivative corrections dominate nonlocal quantum corrections outside large extremal black holes, and what would this imply for the species bound and Weak Gravity Conjecture?

sources.title: Higher derivative corrections to black brane thermodynamics and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Under what conditions do leading higher derivative corrections lower extremal black p-brane tension-to-charge ratios, allowing large branes to satisfy the WGC bound, and how is this related to microcanonical entropy corrections and scattering positivity?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and the Viscosity Bound with Six-Derivative Corrections

evidence.text: Can leading and next-to-leading higher-derivative corrections make the downward extremal mass-to-charge correction associated with the WGC compatible with the KSS viscosity bound for charged AdS5 black branes?

sources.title: Duality and Supersymmetry Constraints on the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can duality symmetries inherited from the UV make positivity bounds or the null energy condition sufficient for the mild WGC in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion theory, and how does additional supersymmetry constrain extremality corrections?

sources.title: Higher-order corrections to mass-charge relation of extremal black holes

evidence.text: Do higher-derivative effects lower the extremal mass at fixed gauge charge and produce repulsion? These are separate tests when additional massless fields contribute attractive forces, so the dynamical-dilaton example requires both mass and scalar-charge corrections.

sources.title: Proof of the Weak Gravity Conjecture from Black Hole Entropy

evidence.text: Under what assumptions do higher-dimension operators increase black-hole entropy at fixed mass and charge, and can the resulting coefficient bounds enforce a positive extremality shift and the weak gravity conjecture?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture, RG Flows, and Supersymmetry

evidence.text: Do one-loop RG flows make higher-derivative extremality corrections positive for sufficiently massive dyonic black holes, thereby satisfying the mild WGC? How do additional massless fields and N≥2 supersymmetric couplings change that conclusion?

sources.title: Thermodynamics of 4D Dilatonic Black Holes and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: How do four-derivative corrections change extremal Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton black-hole masses and entropies, and under which UV assumptions do the resulting Wilson-coefficient conditions support the weak WGC?

sources.title: Scalar quasinormal modes in Reissner-Nordström black holes: implications for Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: How do four-derivative Einstein–Maxwell EFT operators shift massless scalar zero-damping modes of nearly extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes, and does an adopted QNM causality criterion select the same Wilson-coefficient combination as the black-hole Weak Gravity Conjecture?

sources.title: Higher-order corrections to mass-charge relation of extremal black holes

evidence.text: Is the observed negative extremal-mass correction universal in quantum gravity, or does another background furnish a counterexample? Suggested tests include non-supersymmetric type II Calabi-Yau black holes and black branes, neither of which is computed here.

sources.title: Entropy Bounds on Effective Field Theory from Rotating Dyonic Black Holes

evidence.text: What field-basis invariant constraints on four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell EFT follow from positive classical Wald-entropy corrections for thermodynamically stable rotating dyonic black holes, and how do these constraints affect extremality and black-hole decay?

sources.title: Black hole extremality in nonlinear electrodynamics: a lesson for weak gravity and Festina Lente bounds

evidence.text: Do nonlinear electromagnetic corrections preserve the WGC-motivated monotonicity of black-hole extremality beyond four-derivative truncation, and how do light charged particles modify Nariai spectra relevant to the Festina Lente bound?

sources.title: The correlation of WGC and hydrodynamics bound with R4 correction in the charged AdS<math altimg="si1.svg"><msub><mrow/><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> black brane

evidence.text: Do higher-curvature corrections produce compatible constraints from the weak gravity conjecture and the KSS viscosity bound for a hyperscaling-violating charged black brane, and can their overlap diagnose candidate UV-completable effective theories?

sources.title: Effective holographic theories of momentum relaxation and violation of conductivity bound

evidence.text: How do symmetry-allowed higher-derivative couplings between charge and homogeneous translation-breaking sectors affect charged black branes and DC transport? Can they invalidate the positive conductivity lower bound of simpler Einstein–Maxwell–scalar models while respecting the constraints examined here?

sources.title: Quantum gravitational corrections to Reissner-Nordström black hole thermodynamics and their implications for the weak gravity conjecture*

evidence.text: Do nonlocal one-loop effects of massless fields lower the mass of RN black holes at fixed charge, produce the superextremal states relevant to the WGC, and relate that shift to thermodynamic stability and logarithmic entropy corrections?

sources.title: Running Love numbers of charged black holes

evidence.text: How do QFT vacuum corrections generate mixed static gravitational and electromagnetic responses of charged black holes, and how does their running change between weak electromagnetic fields and the strong-field regime beyond the field-strength expansion?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture, Central Charges and $\eta/s$

evidence.text: Does an assumed AdS weak gravity conjecture constrain higher-derivative couplings sufficiently to enforce the KSS bound at extremality, and how do these constraints interact with holographic central-charge bounds?

sources.title: Causality and quasi-normal modes in the GREFT

evidence.text: How do existing causality constraints restrict GREFT black-hole quasi-normal modes, and what additional coefficient bounds follow from conjecturing that EFT corrections cannot resolvably increase their decay lifetimes?

sources.title: The Black Hole Weak Gravity Conjecture with Multiple Charges

evidence.text: How do local higher-derivative interactions among several Abelian photons and gravity modify a charged, spherically symmetric black-hole background?

sources.title: Running Love numbers and the Effective Field Theory of gravity

evidence.text: How do higher-derivative gravitational EFT operators change black-hole static tidal responses, when are Love numbers constant or running, and can charge enhance their observable effects?

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Entropy and the Weak Gravity Conjecture in Anti-de Sitter Space

evidence.text: How do four-derivative interactions change AdS-Reissner-Nordström extremality and microcanonical entropy, and what Wilson-coefficient constraints follow if entropy corrections are positive for thermodynamically stable black holes?

sources.title: Derivative corrections to extremal black holes with moduli

evidence.text: How do higher-derivative operators change the fixed-charge mass, entropy and long-range self-force of large extremal black holes with moduli, and are the three corrections correlated in ways relevant to the WGC and RFC?

sources.title: Repulsive black holes and higher-derivatives

evidence.text: How do four-derivative corrections change the long-range static force between extremal black holes with massless scalars, and when do superextremality and self-repulsion impose different conditions?

sources.title: Sudden breakdown of effective field theory near cool Kerr-Newman black holes

evidence.text: How do leading higher-derivative Einstein-Maxwell corrections change extremal and near-extremal Kerr-Newman horizons, and can enhanced tidal forces arise before low-temperature Schwarzian quantum effects become important?

sources.title: Causality constraints on black hole thermodynamics in nonlinear electrodynamics

evidence.text: What monotonicity properties of charged-black-hole extremality and entropy follow from the paper's subluminality-motivated condition on nonlinear electrodynamics, beyond leading four-derivative corrections?

sources.title: Force-free higher derivative Einstein-Maxwell theory and multi-centered black holes

evidence.text: Which four-derivative Einstein–Maxwell interactions admit static multicentered extremal black holes with position-independent energy, and are their force-free constraints stronger than preservation of the extremal mass–charge ratio?

sources.title: The weak gravity conjecture in the Vilkovisky-DeWitt effective action of quantum gravity

evidence.text: What leading quantum-gravitational correction does the Vilkovisky–DeWitt effective action predict for the extremal Reissner–Nordström mass–charge relation when both local and nonlocal operators are retained, and how can this inform a weak-gravity diagnostic?

sources.title: EFT corrections to charged black hole quasinormal modes

evidence.text: How do higher-derivative Einstein–Maxwell EFT corrections change charged black-hole quasinormal frequencies, especially near extremality, and do calculable electron-induced corrections satisfy the proposed QNM causality bound?

sources.title: Deformations of extremal black holes and the UV

evidence.text: Do UV corrections controlling marginal tidal deformations of extremal charged black holes indicate EFT failure, or faithfully reproduce UV physics? Can their signs motivate gravitational consistency bounds beyond the asymptotically flat weak gravity conjecture (WGC)?

sources.title: α′-corrections to near extremal dyonic strings and weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can higher-derivative corrections to near-extremal forces provide a WGC-motivated consistency criterion when supersymmetry protects the extremal mass-to-charge ratio? How does the answer depend on the thermodynamic quantities held fixed?

sources.title: Extremal Love: tidal/electromagnetic deformability, logarithmic running and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: How do leading four-derivative corrections change the static electromagnetic and gravitational responses of extremal electrically charged black holes, and what restrictions do unitarity and the WGC impose on susceptibilities and logarithmic running?

sources.title: Causality, unitarity, and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Under what assumptions do causality and unitarity constrain higher-derivative corrections to black-hole extremality so that black holes themselves can supply the superextremal states required by the weak gravity conjecture?

sources.title: New cosmological constraints on primordial black holes

evidence.text: How do quark/gluon emission and updated light-element and photon-background observations constrain the initial PBH abundance over 10^9–10^17 g? The paper also reviews constraints extending to much larger, nonevaporating PBHs.

sources.title: Primordial Black Hole production in Critical Higgs Inflation

evidence.text: Can critical Higgs inflation, including running of both the Higgs self-coupling and its non-minimal gravitational coupling, produce enough primordial black holes to explain dark matter while satisfying CMB and particle-physics constraints?

sources.title: On the Limits of Effective Quantum Field Theory: Eternal Inflation, Landscapes, and Other Mythical Beasts

evidence.text: Can the primordial HST black-hole gas evolve into a surviving mass distribution consistent with observations and potentially supply dark matter?

sources.title: Black hole mergers in holographic space time models of cosmology

evidence.text: Do black holes in the early matter-dominated era of HST inflation models merge into sufficiently long-lived objects to violate observational constraints, and can their groups instead form bound structures before evaporation?

sources.title: Through the looking glass into the dark dimension: Searching for bulk black hole dark matter with microlensing of <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e142"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi></math>-ray pulsars

evidence.text: Can X-ray pulsar microlensing probe primordial black holes propagating in the dark-dimension bulk, including masses whose all-dark-matter interpretation is excluded for ordinary evaporating four-dimensional Schwarzschild black holes?

sources.title: New cosmological constraints on primordial black holes

evidence.text: The extragalactic photon calculation integrates evolving PBH emission over cosmic time with redshift and propagation limits. Abundance caps touch upper 1σ observational error tips; known astrophysical contributions are not subtracted.

sources.title: Primordial Black Hole production in Critical Higgs Inflation

evidence.text: The authors compute exact inflationary background evolution and scan (β,ξ₀,x_c,c), choosing λ₀ to match the observed CMB scalar amplitude. They examine n_s, its running and r together with the height and width of the small-scale peak.

sources.title: On the Limits of Effective Quantum Field Theory: Eternal Inflation, Landscapes, and Other Mythical Beasts

evidence.text: Estimate horizon-mediated R violation using a massive-particle round trip and a random walk over horizon degrees of freedom, then seek a self-consistent vanishing mass at infinite dS radius. The source explicitly presents this as a heuristic mechanism.

sources.title: Black hole mergers in holographic space time models of cosmology

evidence.text: Use a rudimentary N-body calculation with classical gravitational accelerations and leapfrog position/velocity updates. Black holes start on a regular lattice with random masses and velocities, while periodic boundary images approximate a three-torus.

sources.title: Through the looking glass into the dark dimension: Searching for bulk black hole dark matter with microlensing of <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e142"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi></math>-ray pulsars

evidence.text: Compares the Einstein radius with the compactification scale and the projected source size. Includes point-source wave optics through a confluent-hypergeometric magnification formula and its small-w limit.

sources.title: New cosmological constraints on primordial black holes

evidence.text: PYTHIA Monte Carlo fragmentation supplies injected hadron and photon energy spectra, including photons from unstable hadrons and fragmentation bremsstrahlung.

sources.title: Constraining primordial black holes as dark matter using the global 21-cm signal with X-ray heating and excess radio background

evidence.text: How does fitting the full EDGES absorption profile, including astrophysical X-ray heating and an excess radio background, constrain evaporating PBHs as dark matter and, conditionally, the small-scale primordial curvature spectrum?

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes as a dark matter candidate

evidence.text: How can primordial black holes form, what limits their present dark-matter abundance, and which mass ranges and theoretical questions remain open? The review targets the status circa Summer 2020; the supplied version is dated December 2020.

sources.title: A brief review on primordial black holes as dark matter

evidence.text: How do primordial black holes form and acquire their abundance and mass distribution, and which evaporation, accretion, gravitational, and cosmological signatures constrain their contribution to dark matter?

sources.title: Primordial black holes from single field models of inflation

evidence.text: Can a single-field inflationary potential generate sufficiently enhanced small-scale curvature fluctuations to produce primordial black holes constituting all dark matter, while retaining agreement with the paper's CMB and LSS constraints?

sources.title: Primordial black hole dark matter from catastrogenesis with unstable pseudo-Goldstone bosons

evidence.text: Can biased string-wall network annihilation produce all dark matter as asteroid-mass primordial black holes when the associated heavy pseudo-Goldstone bosons decay rapidly, and can the accompanying gravitational waves be observable?

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter: Recent Developments

evidence.text: Under which formation scenarios and observational caveats could primordial black holes provide some or all dark matter, explain astrophysical anomalies, or coexist with particle dark matter?

sources.title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap

evidence.text: Which theoretical uncertainties limit predictions of primordial-black-hole abundance, clustering, and merger populations, and which future observations could distinguish a primordial component or test PBH dark matter?

sources.title: Primordial black hole tower: Dark matter, earth-mass, and LIGO black holes

evidence.text: Which PBH masses and fractions could address the adopted dark-matter, GW150914, and OGLE interpretations while avoiding the bounds available to the authors?

sources.title: Primordial black holes are five dimensional

evidence.text: Within the Dark Dimension Scenario, must PBHs from established production mechanisms become five-dimensional, independently of abundance, and can their evaporation occur near the present epoch?

sources.title: Secondary gravitational wave signatures from 5D rotating primordial black holes in the dark dimension

evidence.text: Can rotating five-dimensional primordial black holes survive as dark matter in the Dark Dimension scenario, and can their formation-associated scalar-induced gravitational waves constrain their properties and memory-burden evaporation?

evidence.text: Estimates thermal freeze-out using ⟨σv⟩=a+b⟨v²⟩+O(⟨v⁴⟩), summing the electron-pair and two-exphoton channels in a and b. The reported leading hidden-channel coefficient is a₂γex=πα_ex²/mχ².

sources.title: Galactic 511 keV line from MeV milli-charged dark matter

evidence.text: Factors the annihilation flux into particle-physics terms and a density-squared line-of-sight integral J. Incorporates positronium branching into a 0.275 factor in the 511 keV flux expression, and overlays the inferred charge band with laboratory and cosmological exclusions.

sources.title: Galactic 511 keV line from MeV milli-charged dark matter

evidence.text: Diagonalizes and normalizes the two Abelian kinetic terms, then calculates tree-level annihilation cross sections into e⁺e⁻, two exphotons, photon–exphoton and two photons. Velocity expansions organize the nonrelativistic annihilation rates.
